dd_title: SplitCam Data Deletion — Remove Your Account Data
dd_desc: How to delete the Facebook, YouTube, Twitch and Kick data SplitCam keeps on your phone and revoke its access — in the app, on each platform or by email.
dd_keywords: splitcam data deletion, delete splitcam data, remove splitcam facebook access, splitcam revoke access, splitcam account data
dd_sub: SplitCam keeps the data of your connected accounts only on your device. Here is how to delete it and revoke SplitCam's access at any time.
dd_body:
1. Remove it from the app

  • Open SplitCam → tap + (Channels) → open the channel → Delete channel.
  • Or uninstall SplitCam — this deletes all its data from the device.

2. Revoke SplitCam's access on Facebook

  • Facebook → Settings & privacy → Settings → Business integrations (or Apps and websites) → SplitCam Live Streaming → Remove.
  • You can also delete the posts, videos and events SplitCam published on your timeline or Page (for example, recordings of your live broadcasts). Recordings stay on Facebook until you delete them there.

3. Other platforms

  • YouTube: myaccount.google.com → Security & sign-in → Your connections to third-party apps & services → SplitCam → Remove access.
  • Twitch: Settings → Connections → SplitCam → Disconnect.
  • Kick: Settings → Connections → SplitCam → Disconnect.

Request deletion by email

If you cannot do the steps above, write to support@splitcam.com with the subject “Data deletion” and the name of your account. We will confirm deletion within 30 days. SplitCam servers do not store your account data, so in most cases steps 1–2 are all that is needed.

See also our Privacy Policy. MyDocs Ltd.
pp_section:
Signing in with streaming platforms

The SplitCam mobile app lets you connect your accounts on streaming platforms (Facebook, YouTube, Twitch, Kick) so it can start live broadcasts and show your live chat. When you connect an account, the platform shows you exactly which permissions SplitCam asks for, and you can decline any of them.

What we receive from Facebook

If you sign in with Facebook, SplitCam receives your name, profile picture and an app-specific user ID; the list of Facebook Pages you chose to share with SplitCam and an access token for each of them; and an access token for your account. With your permission SplitCam uses them only to:

  • create a live video on your profile or on a Page you selected, send the video stream to it, and end it when you stop the broadcast;
  • read comments on that live video and show them in the SplitCam chat;
  • post a comment from your Page when you reply in the SplitCam chat.

SplitCam does not read your posts, photos, friends or messages, does not post anything on your behalf except the live video and the replies you type yourself, and does not use Facebook data for advertising.

Where it is stored

Account names, pictures and access tokens are stored only in the app's private storage on your device. They are not sent to SplitCam servers and are not included in device backups. Your video normally goes directly from your phone to each platform. Only if you choose the Restream mode and stream to several platforms at once, the video and the stream key of each destination go through the SplitCam relay server, which forwards the video to the platforms. The sign-in page splitcam.com/auth only hands the one-time sign-in code back to the app; the code is not stored by SplitCam and cannot be reused.

How long

Until you remove the channel in the app, sign out, or uninstall the app. Access tokens also expire, and you can revoke them at any time on the platform side.

Other services in the app

The app uses Firebase Crashlytics (crash reports) and Firebase Analytics (anonymous usage statistics) by Google. The Facebook SDK is used only for sign-in; its automatic event logging and advertising ID collection are turned off.

Deleting your data

See Data deletion — how to remove your data from the app and revoke SplitCam's access on each platform.
